From catalogue to ecosystem, an immersive 3D experience designed to show not just what Omnicell sells, but how everything connects
Creative Strategy & Vision, art direction, UX & UI
Immersive 3D, WebGL, Interactive Storytelling, Brand Experience
How do you show a product network, not just a product list?

Omnicell's portfolio is vast, automation, replenishment, data, traceability, distribution. But the real story wasn't in the products. It was in how they work together. The brief was clear: replace a 60-page catalogue with something that could actually show the network

Zoom out first. 
Then let them dive in.

The strategy was built around one principle, give users a panoramic view first, then let them go deeper.

We designed three levels of reading: the full hospital ecosystem from above, a product-level exploration, and workflow-based journeys that show how everything operates as a network. The entry point doesn't matter — every path leads back to the whole.

The process was about making complexity navigable. We designed the hospital environment from scratch in 3D, placing each product in its real context, pharmacy, ward, operating room. Connection arcs make the network visible at a glance. 

Hotspots open product panels without leaving the space. Workflow modes move the camera through role-based journeys, turning a static catalogue into a guided experience. Multiple entry points, one coherent world.
Built for the web.  Used everywhere.

The result is an experience that works at every scale — on a screen, on a stand, in a sales meeting. What started as a web platform quickly became Omnicell's go-to sales tool, used by their teams across trade shows and client presentations to walk prospects through the full ecosystem in real time.

The shift from document to experience changed how the product is sold. Complex becomes clear. The network becomes visible. And every conversation starts from the same panoramic view of what Omnicell actually offers.

The experience wasn't just built for the web, it was built to travel. From standalone web exploration to trade show booths and live sales presentations, it adapted to every context without losing its clarity. Hospital buyers could explore at their own pace. Sales teams could guide the conversation. The same panoramic view, the same depth, wherever the meeting happened.

Raw materials carry their own narratives, shaped by origin, transformation and time

Wood, rock, metal, and water were approached not as neutral elements but as forms already marked by their journey.
Each material reflects where it comes from and what it has become, forming the foundation of the visual story.
Creation begins at the meeting point between artist and material

Through interaction and intent, both shape one another, giving rise to a new form.

From product range to living ecosystem, an immersive 3D city designed to show not just what Renault Trucks makes, but how its vehicles keep cities moving
How do you show a product ecosystem, not just a fleet?

Renault Trucks’ range spans construction, logistics, delivery, waste collection and essential urban services. But the real story wasn’t in the vehicles alone. It was in where they operate, what they enable and how deeply they are woven into the daily life of modern cities.

The brief was to turn that ecosystem into an immersive communication and marketing tool, one that could speak to the general public, city officials and industry professionals alike.

The strategy was built around one principle: put the vehicles in context.

Instead of presenting Renault Trucks as a catalogue of products, we created a dynamic 3D city where every neighborhood reveals a different part of the ecosystem. Visitors explore the city first, then dive into real-world use cases, from package delivery and infrastructure work to refuse collection.

Every route leads back to the same idea: Renault Trucks is part of how a modern city works.

We designed the city as a living environment, placing specialized vehicles directly inside the situations they were built for.

Points of interest turn the map into an interactive layer of discovery. Visitors move between neighborhoods, explore different urban services and see Renault Trucks vehicles at the heart of the action.

Rather than separating technical product information from its application, the experience brings the two together, transforming complexity into something playful, intuitive and easy to navigate.

Built for the web.
Designed to go further.

The result is an immersive experience built with WebGL and real-time 3D, designed to run smoothly across desktop and mobile.

But the platform was never limited to individual web exploration. It was also used as a centerpiece at high-profile events such as the Salon de l’Automobile, giving audiences an engaging and futuristic way into the Renault Trucks universe.

Through interactive storytelling, the experience captures attention, informs audiences and gives the brand a bold, modern format for communicating its value.

Different people.
Different needs.
One city.

The virtual city was designed to work for different people in different contexts.

The general public can discover the role trucks play in everyday urban life. City officials can explore the services and infrastructure they support. Industry professionals can understand fleet solutions through real-world applications rather than isolated specifications.

The same city, the same ecosystem, different ways in.
By turning the product range into an explorable world, the experience positions Renault Trucks not just as a manufacturer, but as a key player in the future of urban living.
A whole city, across every screen

The platform was built using WebGL and real-time 3D rendering to maintain a smooth, immersive experience across devices, including mobile.

The challenge wasn’t simply to make the city fit on a smaller screen. It was to preserve the clarity of the exploration, the impact of the 3D world and the accessibility of the product information wherever the experience was opened.

One ecosystem. Every screen.
We mapped Renault Trucks’ ecosystem and built the concept around one idea: placing each vehicle in context, showing how they work together to keep a city moving.
A playful, stylized visual language designed to make a complex range of vehicles and urban applications feel accessible, cohesive and instantly recognizable.
A complete 3D city built around real-world use cases, from construction and infrastructure to delivery, logistics and waste collection, optimized for real-time exploration.
A non-linear experience that lets visitors move freely through the city, discover points of interest and explore Renault Trucks vehicles through the situations they were designed for.
A WebGL experience designed for smooth real-time 3D exploration across desktop and mobile, balancing visual richness, performance and accessibility.

From skincare to scientific storytelling, an immersive 3D experience designed to reveal not just what the product does, but why and how it works
How do you make skincare science engaging?

Launching Active Recovery Body Milk meant communicating a sophisticated formula without overwhelming users with technical information.

The challenge was to transform scientific credibility into an experience that felt intuitive, immersive and easy to understand, while remaining accessible across every device.

Start with the science.
Turn it into discovery.

Rather than presenting product claims through a traditional landing page, we built an interactive visual website where every scroll reveals another layer of the formula.

Scientific ingredients, product benefits and practical applications are woven together through storytelling, allowing users to understand the product by exploring it.

Every interaction reinforces the same message: innovation is easier to trust when you can visualise it.

The experience was built around detailed 3D visualization and purposeful interaction.

Precise animations, realistic materials and interactive sequences explain how the active ingredients work and why they matter. Instead of simplifying the science, the experience makes it easier to navigate.

The interface was intentionally designed to remain clean, focused and effortless, allowing the product to take center stage.

Built to educate. 
Designed to captivate.

The result is an immersive WebGL experience that combines product storytelling with scientific visualization. 

As users progress through the journey, they discover the formula, understand its benefits and connect each ingredient to real-world results. Visual storytelling transforms technical information into an engaging experience without sacrificing clarity. 

The platform becomes more than a product launch. It becomes a tool for education, engagement and brand storytelling.

Whether experienced on desktop, tablet or mobile, the experience maintains the same clarity and visual impact.

Every interaction, animation and piece of content adapts seamlessly across devices, ensuring users can discover the product with the same fluidity wherever they are.

One story. Every screen.
We built the experience around one simple idea: transforming skincare science into an story that anyone can understand

From fragrance to experience, an immersive 3D garden designed to reveal not just what goes into a scent, but the stories, ingredients and craft behind it
Concept Development, Art Direction, 3D Design, Motion Graphics, UX Design, Interactive Design
How do you make a fragrance explorable?

Fragrance is intimate, sensory and deeply personal. Translating that into a digital experience means working without the one sense that defines it most: smell.

The challenge was to create a new kind of connection with Maison Margiela’s audience, bringing the ingredients, stories and creative processes behind its fragrances to life through interaction and visual.

The brief was to make the invisible feel tangible.

Enter the garden first.
Then discover what lies within.

The strategy was built around immersion. Rather than presenting the fragrances as products, we invited users into the world they come from.

We created the Margiela Garden, a 3D environment where plants, ingredients and stories become part of the landscape. Users could wander freely, discover the origins of each fragrance and gradually dive deeper into the creative process.

Every interaction reveals another layer of the Maison Margiela universe.
Make scent something you can explore

The process was about translating an olfactory world into a visual and interactive one.

We built the garden as a space for discovery, combining 3D environments, storytelling, interviews and playful interactions. Exclusive conversations with Maison Margiela’s perfumers reveal the thinking and craft behind each creation, bringing a human voice into the experience.

Interactive mini-games invite users to experiment with ingredients such as mandarin and patchouli leaves, turning fragrance composition into something playful and intuitive.

A garden to explore.
A story to collect.

The result is an immersive journey where exploration becomes part of the storytelling.

As users move through the garden, they uncover ingredients, encounter stories and collect digital Polaroids that capture moments from their journey. These virtual keepsakes introduce a nostalgic layer inspired by memory, encouraging users to keep exploring.

Storytelling, interaction and visual elegance come together to transform fragrance discovery into something personal, engaging and memorable.

The Margiela Garden was designed to retain its character wherever it was experienced.

On desktop, users can immerse themselves in the full 3D environment. On mobile, the experience adapts while preserving the same sense of exploration, interaction and visual detail.

The same garden, the same stories, the same poetic universe, wherever the journey begins.
We translated Maison Margiela’s olfactory universe into an interactive world, building the concept around one idea: making fragrance discoverable through the ingredients, stories and people behind it

Caricatures of two US presidential candidates on a red flag against a starry background, from the Unpresidential satirical game
Concept Development, Art Direction, 3D & Motion Design
Commissioned by Bright Studio, we conceptualized and developed a satirical video game built around the 2020 US elections
After conducting research on both candidates, our initial step was brainstorming ideas for special moves that aligned with the political agendas and beliefs of Trump and Biden
For Trump, we envisioned moves such as "Heatwave" featuring burning trees to symbolize his climate change denial, or an attack involving a flock of blue birds to represent his "Excessive Tweeting"
The gameplay of "Unpresidential!" draws inspiration from casual fighting games commonly found on different video game platforms

Featuring an array of special moves like "Tweet Salvo!", "Russian Collusion", "Mega MAGA!", "Working Class Joe", and "Unavoidable Tax!", "Unpresidential!" offers players a humorous and absurd exploration of the programs and politics of each White House contender

Every action, whether it's a regular shot, a special move, or the outcome of a game, is accompanied by witty jokes related to the candidate's life or platform, delivered by talented voice impersonators

Additionally, "Special Events" can occur randomly during gameplay, such as "Coronavirus!" or "Impeachment!", during which players must execute a series of moves to unleash a "Mega Attack" like "Mega MAGA!" for Trump or "Obama Bromance!"

The game was planned to receive ongoing updates with fresh content, including new locations like a political rally in a stadium, the UN Headquarters, or the Oval Office. Moreover, new characters with unique abilities such as Bernie Sanders, Kamala Harris, and Barack Obama were set to be introduced to enhance replayability

Imagined and built with Bright Studio, we created a digital town for Sopra Banking Software — a welcoming hub giving collaborators access to exclusive content during a live event

We started the project by adopting a straightforward concept: allowing each user to design a ship inspired by the new SBS logo. This personalized element served as a creative and symbolic entry point into the experience. With their custom vessel, users would traverse a linear world, encountering a series of sculptures that embodied the event's central themes.

These sculptures acted as visual touchpoints, guiding users through the narrative of the event. To enhance engagement, we introduced a collectible feature, enabling users to track the objects and themes they encountered. This addition created a sense of progression and achievement, enriching the overall experience.
Following initial discussions with the client, it became clear they were seeking a more ambitious and expansive concept.

The idea of a digital city resonated strongly with them, aligning seamlessly with their live event program and offering an ideal solution.
The concept provided attendees with a preview of the live event within the platform while also allowing them to explore its themes through a metaphorical and interactive representation. This approach fostered a more immersive and engaging virtual presence, bridging the gap between the digital and live experiences.
This digital town was meticulously crafted, featuring distinct districts, each dedicated to showcasing a specific theme tied to the event.
Users could navigate freely through the town using drag-and-drop functionality or explore it from a structured perspective via a top-view “City Map”.

Each district was uniquely designed, with buildings inspired by renowned architects like Shigeru Ban. This architectural diversity not only elevated the town’s visual appeal but also enriched its thematic storytelling.
During the onboarding process, participants are invited to personalize their experience by designing their own avatars.
This customization adds a dynamic and engaging layer to the digital experience, fostering a sense of individuality and connection within the virtual environment.

A collective 3D fan experience created to celebrate Assassin’s Creed’s anniversary, bringing thousands of players together to create a shared digital monument to the franchise
How do you turn a franchise anniversary into a shared experience?
Fifteen years of Assassin’s Creed meant fifteen years of stories, characters and memories shared by a global community.
The challenge was to create a digital celebration that could bring that community together — not simply to revisit the franchise, but to actively become part of its legacy.
The idea was simple: give every fan a piece of the celebration.

Make the community part
of the monument

At the centre of the experience sits a 3D sculpture of an Assassin’s Creed character. The sculpture is progressively assembled as fans claim individual pieces, turning the audience into participants in the creation of a shared digital monument. Every contribution becomes part of the whole. The anniversary wasn't something to watch. It was something to build together.
Fans from across the Assassin’s Creed community could claim one of 100,000 available pieces and contribute to the construction of the sculpture.
As participation grew, so did the monument — gradually transforming from an individual collection of pieces into a collective representation of the franchise and its community.

The experience wasn't just built for the web, it was built to travel. From standalone web exploration to trade show booths and live sales presentations, it adapted to every context without losing its clarity.

We translated Assassin’s Creed’s 15-year legacy into a collective digital experience, building the concept around one idea: giving every fan a piece of the monument and making them part of its creation.
A visual experience built around the scale and mythology of the Assassin’s Creed universe, with the central sculpture serving as the focal point of the celebration.
A real-time 3D sculpture designed as the core of a collective digital monument, progressively assembled through fan participation.
An exploration-based experience where users could discover designated areas, claim individual pieces and become part of the final creation.
A WebGL experience developed with Vue.js, designed to bring the interactive 3D environment to the web.

Aerial view of a 3D virtual city built to showcase the Renault Trucks product and service ecosystem
From product range to living ecosystem, an immersive 3D city designed to show not just what Renault Trucks makes, but how its vehicles keep cities moving
How do you show a product ecosystem, not just a fleet?

Renault Trucks’ range spans construction, logistics, delivery, waste collection and essential urban services. But the real story wasn’t in the vehicles alone. It was in where they operate, what they enable and how deeply they are woven into the daily life of modern cities.

The brief was to turn that ecosystem into an immersive communication and marketing tool, one that could speak to the general public, city officials and industry professionals alike.

The strategy was built around one principle: put the vehicles in context.

Instead of presenting Renault Trucks as a catalogue of products, we created a dynamic 3D city where every neighborhood reveals a different part of the ecosystem. Visitors explore the city first, then dive into real-world use cases, from package delivery and infrastructure work to refuse collection.

Every route leads back to the same idea: Renault Trucks is part of how a modern city works.

We designed the city as a living environment, placing specialized vehicles directly inside the situations they were built for.

Points of interest turn the map into an interactive layer of discovery. Visitors move between neighborhoods, explore different urban services and see Renault Trucks vehicles at the heart of the action.

Rather than separating technical product information from its application, the experience brings the two together, transforming complexity into something playful, intuitive and easy to navigate.

Built for the web.
Designed to go further.

The result is an immersive experience built with WebGL and real-time 3D, designed to run smoothly across desktop and mobile.

But the platform was never limited to individual web exploration. It was also used as a centerpiece at high-profile events such as the Salon de l’Automobile, giving audiences an engaging and futuristic way into the Renault Trucks universe.

Through interactive storytelling, the experience captures attention, informs audiences and gives the brand a bold, modern format for communicating its value.

Different people.
Different needs.
One city.

The virtual city was designed to work for different people in different contexts.

The general public can discover the role trucks play in everyday urban life. City officials can explore the services and infrastructure they support. Industry professionals can understand fleet solutions through real-world applications rather than isolated specifications.

The same city, the same ecosystem, different ways in.
By turning the product range into an explorable world, the experience positions Renault Trucks not just as a manufacturer, but as a key player in the future of urban living.
A whole city, across every screen

The platform was built using WebGL and real-time 3D rendering to maintain a smooth, immersive experience across devices, including mobile.

The challenge wasn’t simply to make the city fit on a smaller screen. It was to preserve the clarity of the exploration, the impact of the 3D world and the accessibility of the product information wherever the experience was opened.

One ecosystem. Every screen.
We mapped Renault Trucks’ ecosystem and built the concept around one idea: placing each vehicle in context, showing how they work together to keep a city moving.
A playful, stylized visual language designed to make a complex range of vehicles and urban applications feel accessible, cohesive and instantly recognizable.
A complete 3D city built around real-world use cases, from construction and infrastructure to delivery, logistics and waste collection, optimized for real-time exploration.
A non-linear experience that lets visitors move freely through the city, discover points of interest and explore Renault Trucks vehicles through the situations they were designed for.
A WebGL experience designed for smooth real-time 3D exploration across desktop and mobile, balancing visual richness, performance and accessibility.
Development was executed in partnership with Bright.

How do you make a fragrance explorable?

Fragrance is intimate, sensory and deeply personal. Translating that into a digital experience means working without the one sense that defines it most: smell.

The challenge was to create a new kind of connection with Maison Margiela’s audience, bringing the ingredients, stories and creative processes behind its fragrances to life through interaction and visual.

The brief was to make the invisible feel tangible.

Enter the garden first.
Then discover what lies within.

The strategy was built around immersion. Rather than presenting the fragrances as products, we invited users into the world they come from.

We created the Margiela Garden, a 3D environment where plants, ingredients and stories become part of the landscape. Users could wander freely, discover the origins of each fragrance and gradually dive deeper into the creative process.

Every interaction reveals another layer of the Maison Margiela universe.
Make scent something you can explore

The process was about translating an olfactory world into a visual and interactive one.

We built the garden as a space for discovery, combining 3D environments, storytelling, interviews and playful interactions. Exclusive conversations with Maison Margiela’s perfumers reveal the thinking and craft behind each creation, bringing a human voice into the experience.

Interactive mini-games invite users to experiment with ingredients such as mandarin and patchouli leaves, turning fragrance composition into something playful and intuitive.

A garden to explore.
A story to collect.

The result is an immersive journey where exploration becomes part of the storytelling.

As users move through the garden, they uncover ingredients, encounter stories and collect digital Polaroids that capture moments from their journey. These virtual keepsakes introduce a nostalgic layer inspired by memory, encouraging users to keep exploring.

Storytelling, interaction and visual elegance come together to transform fragrance discovery into something personal, engaging and memorable.

The Margiela Garden was designed to retain its character wherever it was experienced.

Caricatures of two US presidential candidates on a red flag against a starry background, from the Unpresidential satirical game
Concept Development, Art Direction, 3D & Motion Design
Commissioned by Bright Studio, we conceptualized and developed a satirical video game built around the 2020 US elections
After conducting research on both candidates, our initial step was brainstorming ideas for special moves that aligned with the political agendas and beliefs of Trump and Biden
For Trump, we envisioned moves such as "Heatwave" featuring burning trees to symbolize his climate change denial, or an attack involving a flock of blue birds to represent his "Excessive Tweeting"
The gameplay of "Unpresidential!" draws inspiration from casual fighting games commonly found on different video game platforms

Featuring an array of special moves like "Tweet Salvo!", "Russian Collusion", "Mega MAGA!", "Working Class Joe", and "Unavoidable Tax!", "Unpresidential!" offers players a humorous and absurd exploration of the programs and politics of each White House contender

Every action, whether it's a regular shot, a special move, or the outcome of a game, is accompanied by witty jokes related to the candidate's life or platform, delivered by talented voice impersonators

Additionally, "Special Events" can occur randomly during gameplay, such as "Coronavirus!" or "Impeachment!", during which players must execute a series of moves to unleash a "Mega Attack" like "Mega MAGA!" for Trump or "Obama Bromance!"

The game was planned to receive ongoing updates with fresh content, including new locations like a political rally in a stadium, the UN Headquarters, or the Oval Office. Moreover, new characters with unique abilities such as Bernie Sanders, Kamala Harris, and Barack Obama were set to be introduced to enhance replayability

Neon-lit 3D digital town with glowing geometric buildings, created for Sopra Banking Software's live event
Imagined and built with Bright Studio, we created a digital town for Sopra Banking Software — a welcoming hub giving collaborators access to exclusive content during a live event

We started the project by adopting a straightforward concept: allowing each user to design a ship inspired by the new SBS logo. This personalized element served as a creative and symbolic entry point into the experience. With their custom vessel, users would traverse a linear world, encountering a series of sculptures that embodied the event's central themes.

These sculptures acted as visual touchpoints, guiding users through the narrative of the event. To enhance engagement, we introduced a collectible feature, enabling users to track the objects and themes they encountered. This addition created a sense of progression and achievement, enriching the overall experience.
Following initial discussions with the client, it became clear they were seeking a more ambitious and expansive concept.

The idea of a digital city resonated strongly with them, aligning seamlessly with their live event program and offering an ideal solution.
The concept provided attendees with a preview of the live event within the platform while also allowing them to explore its themes through a metaphorical and interactive representation. This approach fostered a more immersive and engaging virtual presence, bridging the gap between the digital and live experiences.
This digital town was meticulously crafted, featuring distinct districts, each dedicated to showcasing a specific theme tied to the event.
Users could navigate freely through the town using drag-and-drop functionality or explore it from a structured perspective via a top-view “City Map”.

Each district was uniquely designed, with buildings inspired by renowned architects like Shigeru Ban. This architectural diversity not only elevated the town’s visual appeal but also enriched its thematic storytelling.
During the onboarding process, participants are invited to personalize their experience by designing their own avatars.
This customization adds a dynamic and engaging layer to the digital experience, fostering a sense of individuality and connection within the virtual environment.

Fifteen years of Assassin’s Creed meant fifteen years of stories, characters and memories shared by a global community.
The challenge was to create a digital celebration that could bring that community together — not simply to revisit the franchise, but to actively become part of its legacy.
The idea was simple: give every fan a piece of the celebration.

Make the community part
of the monument

At the centre of the experience sits a 3D sculpture of an Assassin’s Creed character. The sculpture is progressively assembled as fans claim individual pieces, turning the audience into participants in the creation of a shared digital monument. Every contribution becomes part of the whole. The anniversary wasn't something to watch. It was something to build together.
Fans from across the Assassin’s Creed community could claim one of 100,000 available pieces and contribute to the construction of the sculpture.
As participation grew, so did the monument — gradually transforming from an individual collection of pieces into a collective representation of the franchise and its community.
